review_policy.reason: A second independent source review has not occurred.

audit_units.scope_note: The traced path compiles constraints from the user query and audits proposed tool name/arguments before runtime execution.
audit_units.finding: At the fixed commit, the inspected VIGIL path derives constraints from user_query and passes only tool-call identity and arguments into RuntimeAuditor. No evaluator label or answer-key parameter is present at those online boundaries.
audit_units.limitations: No paid model call was executed. Constraint quality and uninspected enhanced paths remain outside this unit; an independent second reviewer is still required.

audit_units.scope_note: The fixed public VIGIL checkout does not contain a file or directory named for SIREN, so a loader-to-guard trace cannot be completed from this artifact.
audit_units.finding: The official repository commit is pinned, but no SIREN loader/evaluator implementation is present under the inspected checkout. This unit is completed as inconclusive rather than inferred from the paper.
audit_units.limitations: No source-level claim about SIREN online visibility is allowed until the benchmark implementation is released or another official artifact is identified.

audit_units.component: planner, dynamic validator, and injection isolator
audit_units.scope_note: The DRIFT guard receives the original query, tool definitions, trajectory/checklist state and tool messages; the task suite computes utility/security after the pipeline returns.
audit_units.finding: No evaluator result or injection-task identity is referenced by the inspected DRIFTLLM online validation boundaries. Utility/security are computed in DRIFTTaskSuite after agent execution.
audit_units.limitations: The repository bundles historical result files and AgentDojo-derived code. This unit covers the named DRIFTLLM path only and has not run a paid model.

audit_units.scope_note: TaskSuite owns task objects and evaluators, while AgentPipeline.query receives a prompt/runtime/environment projection.
audit_units.finding: The fixed loader/orchestrator retains task objects outside the pipeline call. The online AgentPipeline boundary itself does not accept answer or success fields.
audit_units.limitations: The environment deliberately contains injected content. This finding concerns evaluator/gold separation, not the absence of malicious content.

audit_units.scope_note: ToolFilter asks a model to select from runtime tools using the current conversation and a fixed filtering prompt.
audit_units.finding: No per-case expected tool or evaluator label is present at OpenAILLMToolFilter.query; the selected runtime tool set is derived from messages and tool schemas.
audit_units.limitations: The filter is OpenAI-model-specific in this commit and this audit does not establish security effectiveness.

audit_units.scope_note: The detector sees tool-output text and a fixed detector threshold/model; model class labels are detector outputs, not benchmark gold labels.
audit_units.finding: The online detector is label-independent with respect to benchmark evaluation. Its own model output label and safe_label configuration are intrinsic detector state.
audit_units.limitations: This is detector-only evidence and cannot be equated with runtime authorization or unsafe-effect prevention.

audit_units.scope_note: These functions evaluate completed traces/environments and are not inserted as guard inputs.
audit_units.finding: AgentDojo utility/security methods are post-hoc evaluators. Their access to task definitions is expected and must not be confused with online defense visibility.
audit_units.limitations: This unit does not audit every third-party defense integrated into AgentDojo.

audit_units.component: policy generator and deterministic privilege enforcement
audit_units.scope_note: Policy generation consumes user query/tool schemas; updates may consume tool outputs, and enforcement consumes tool name/kwargs.
audit_units.finding: No evaluator/gold fields are present at the inspected Progent policy/enforcement boundaries. Automatic narrowing is optional via SECAGENT_ONLY_ALLOW_NARROW and is not the default, which remains a material mechanism difference from M3.
audit_units.limitations: No live policy-model request was made. The absent root license and optional rather than default narrowing must be disclosed.

audit_units.scope_note: The live PrivilegedLLM path uses query/runtime/environment, while the optional replay path introspects benchmark stack frames and routes by user/injection task IDs.
audit_units.finding: The live interpreter path does not expose benchmark labels, but replay components explicitly capture user_task_id and injection_task_id to select historical traces. Comparisons must distinguish live CaMeL from replay mode.
audit_units.limitations: Task IDs are not themselves success labels, but they can select case-specific artifacts. A dynamic replay sentinel test and independent review are still required before stronger claims.

audit_units.component: tool dependency graph planner and executor
audit_units.scope_note: The DAG constructor receives user query and runtime tool documentation; benchmark task objects remain in run/eval.py.
audit_units.finding: No evaluator label or expected tool is present in the inspected IPIGuard DAG construction/traversal boundaries.
audit_units.limitations: The pinned implementation previously failed local qualification on unstable DAG JSON. This audit establishes field visibility, not runtime reliability.

audit_units.scope_note: StruQ structures natural-language instruction/data for a model and does not enforce tool authorization.
audit_units.finding: The inspected StruQ code is a prompt-structure/training defense rather than a tool-execution runtime guard. Some attack constructors use reference outputs to craft completion attacks, which is attack generation rather than online authorization.
audit_units.limitations: StruQ remains relevant to prompt injection but is not comparable to M3's ALLOW/ASK/DENY execution mechanism.

audit_units.component: benchmark loader and online prompt construction
audit_units.scope_note: The prompted agent receives the user instruction, all available tool descriptions and a scratchpad built from tool observations.
audit_units.finding: The model-call boundary does not consume the evaluator's target tool or eval result. All attacker tools are intentionally available to the agent as benchmark attack surface.
audit_units.limitations: This benchmark does not provide an independent runtime authorization policy and therefore cannot test parameter-level authorization without an adapter.

audit_units.scope_note: The evaluator explicitly receives target_tool and attacker metadata after the model output is produced.
audit_units.finding: InjecAgent answer-key fields are used by post-hoc evaluation functions, not by the inspected model-call boundary.
audit_units.limitations: A future defense adapter must preserve this separation; wrapping the evaluator as a Guard would create oracle leakage.

audit_units.scope_note: The common runtime applies a prompt/context defense before a target LLM query; it does not authorize tool execution.
audit_units.finding: PIArena's BaseDefense boundary is separated from answer evaluators, but it is a prompt-defense runtime rather than an action authorization guard.
audit_units.limitations: Adaptive attack modules may legitimately use attack targets; they are attacker/evaluator components and are outside this defense boundary.

audit_units.scope_note: The registry constructs prompt-defense adapters from a defense name/config and batches target instructions/contexts.
audit_units.finding: No evaluator fields are part of the inspected registry/execute_batch signatures, but these adapters do not implement tool authorization.
audit_units.limitations: Individual third-party defenses registered by PIArena require their own audits before use as formal comparators.

audit_units.scope_note: BIPIA constructs indirect-prompt-injection prompts and model messages; it does not gate tool execution.
audit_units.finding: Prompt construction is separated from reference-response construction, but the artifact is not a runtime authorization guard.
audit_units.limitations: BIPIA can support prompt-injection generalization only; an M3 tool-action adapter would be a new benchmark layer.

audit_units.scope_note: ASB intentionally installs attacker tools/payloads into the online attack environment; this is benchmark construction rather than a defense authorization key.
audit_units.finding: The loader makes attacker tool content visible as attack surface, while attacker_goal is used by post-hoc evaluation. No independent per-case authorization policy is enforced.
audit_units.limitations: ASB is useful for attack generalization and over-blocking analysis but needs an explicit M3 authorization manifest for action-level evaluation.

audit_units.scope_note: The metric helpers consume attacker_goal or the expected normal tool set after execution.
audit_units.finding: ASB answer-key information belongs to post-hoc metrics. It would be oracle leakage only if a defense adapter passed these fields into its online Guard.
audit_units.limitations: The upstream script also reports an ASR excluding workflow failures; paper-v2 must retain such failures in the ITT denominator.

audit_units.component: web-agent benchmark task construction, online agent loop, and evaluator separation
audit_units.scope_note: The archived Meta repository constructs separate user-goal and attacker-goal evaluator task dictionaries. The inspected PromptAgent boundary receives the user intent, trajectory/web observations, prompts and injected content, but not the separate eval dictionaries.
audit_units.finding: WASP is a web-agent attack benchmark, not a tool-authorization defense. Its attacker objective is intentionally embedded in the environment/prompt as attack surface, while user and attacker eval objects are constructed and consumed outside the inspected action-generation boundary.
audit_units.limitations: The repository was archived on 2026-07-01 and uses subproject code derived from WebArena/VisualWebArena. This static audit did not install the web environments, call a model, or establish M3 compatibility.

audit_units.scope_note: Guardian methods format only user request, interaction history, current action and environment/action description. Dataset score is appended after the call.
audit_units.finding: The inspected ToolSafe guard-call payload excludes sample score/label even though the surrounding evaluator later appends sample['score']. This is a valid phase separation at the call boundary.
audit_units.limitations: The repository has no root license file at the fixed commit, and this audit does not reproduce guard-model weights or effectiveness.

audit_units.scope_note: PromptGuard is a text classifier artifact. It does not decide or execute parameter-level tool authorization by itself.
audit_units.finding: PromptGuard must remain detector-only in paper-v2 tables. Its detector scores cannot be reported as unsafe-effect prevention without a separate enforcement policy.
audit_units.limitations: The model artifact has no generic tool-authorization interface; runtime behavior is supplied by the host adapter and requires its own source audit.

audit_units.component: paper-disclosed task alignment and local reproduction boundary
audit_units.scope_note: ACL Anthology and the paper contain no official code link. The inspected Python is this project's explicitly disclosed paper reproduction, hash-bound separately from the official PDF; it is not represented as author code.
audit_units.finding: The local reproduction derives user tasks from the trusted query and checks assistant content/tool proposals against those tasks without evaluator fields. This supports only the local adapter's online projection; the authors' exact implementation remains unavailable for source audit.
audit_units.limitations: No official Task Shield source repository was identified on the ACL or arXiv record. The local reproduction has historical negative qualification evidence and cannot establish source-faithful effectiveness or the authors' implementation details.
